fixes.row: Said as near, or as here: “is near”, “has come upon you”, “in your midst”, “brought us into”, “is being preached”
fixes.why: Rev 1:9 says “partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance”. It does not say the kingdom is near or here, so under this label a reader is told the verse says something it does not. The note’s present-tense sentence leans on it too.
fixes.fix: Move Rev.1.9 to the row “Receive it, inherit it, be given it” (it sits beside Heb 12:28 there, and that row’s label covers “partner in”, or widen that label to “partner in the kingdom”). Delete Rev 1:9 from the note of the near/here row and keep Heb 12:28 and Col 1:13 as its present and past examples.

fixes.row: Reign and kingship: “He must reign”, “He will reign”, “they will reign upon the earth”, “for a thousand years”
fixes.why: The nobleman’s parable has no thousand years and no reign of the saints. Filed under the thousand-years label it implies a link the text does not state, which is the worker’s own contested point 3. Its word is a king’s claim to kingship, which is the sense of the row for a king’s reign.
fixes.fix: Move Luke.19.12, 19.14, 19.15 and 19.27 to the row “A king’s reign, his kingship and what is royal”, and move the parable sentence of the note there too (“a man of noble birth ... to lay claim to his kingship”; “We do not want this man to reign over us”), with the line that the page does not say whom the nobleman stands for. The reign row keeps Rev 20:4, 20:6, 1 Cor 15:25, Rev 11:15 and the rest.

fixes.row: Given, taken away, thrown out, restored: “taken away from you and given to a people”, “restore the kingdom to Israel”, “a kingdom of priests”
fixes.why: Exodus 19:6 is the Sinai word to Israel, and here it sits in a row led by Matt 21:43 “given to a people” and Acts 1:6, so the Hebrew Scriptures are read under a New Testament story. The row’s note says it is one story, which the rabbi would reject. Rule 5 is breached.
fixes.fix: Move Exod.19.6 to the row “Israel’s and Judah’s own kingdom” (row 3), with a note that it is the covenant word to Israel at Sinai and not a monarchy verse. The row keeps Rev.1.6 and Rev.5.10 for “a kingdom of priests”, and its note keeps the “church or Israel” reading. Remove Exod 19:6 from the list of verses given with the phrase in that note.

fixes.row: The LORD’s kingdom, and the LORD over every kingdom: “Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom”, “His kingdom rules over all”, “gives it to whom He wishes”
fixes.why: In Ps 45 the words “Your throne, O God ... the scepter of Your kingdom” are addressed to a king. Under the label “the LORD’s kingdom” the psalm is read as about the LORD, which is the reading of Heb 1:8 and of the Christian seats, and the row takes that side by placement even with the note. The rabbi would see the row settling who the psalm addresses.
fixes.fix: Move Ps.45.6 to the row “One king’s kingdom, realm or sovereignty” (row 2), with the note: “Ps 45:6 (‘Your throne, O God ... the scepter of Your kingdom’) is addressed to a king; Heb 1:8 reads it ‘about the Son’ (in the row of the Son), and readers part on whom the psalm addresses; the page does not choose.” Delete the matching sentence from the LORD row’s note. Heb.1.8 stays in the Son row.

fixes.row: What the text says the kingdom is not: “not with observable signs”, “not of this world”, “not eating and drinking”, “not talk but power”
fixes.why: Luke 17:21 says the kingdom “is in your midst”. It is not a negation, and a reader scanning the “is not” row sees it under a claim it does not make. The worker’s point 11 notes the row could be read as favouring the now-reading; the placement is the cause.
fixes.fix: Remove Luke.17.21 from this row (and its sentence in the note). It stays in the row “Said as near, or as here”, where its label fits, and the “within you” / “in your midst” note stays there.

worker_points.point: 1. Rows 12 and 13: the kingdom now, still to come, or both (Matt 11:12, Luke 16:16, Rev 1:9, Luke 21:31, Luke 17:21)
worker_points.why: Matt 11:12 (“has been suffering violence” until now) and Luke 16:16 (“is being preached”) are present statements and stay. Rev 1:9 says partner in the kingdom and is moved (fix 1). Luke 21:31 says “is near” as written and stays with its note. Luke 17:21 is also moved out of the “is not” row (fix 5).

worker_points.point: 2. Rows 7 and 8: kingdom of heaven and kingdom of God; “in Matthew alone”
worker_points.why: The phrase counts are checked on the build (all 31 heaven verses in Matthew). The note says the page does not call them one and takes no side.

worker_points.point: 3. Row 24: the thousand years, with Luke 19:12-27 in the same row
worker_points.why: The parable is about a nobleman’s kingship and says nothing of a thousand years, so it implies a link the text does not state (fix 2).

worker_points.point: 4. Rows 5 and 6: Daniel, Dan 2:44 and 7:14 in both rows
worker_points.why: A verse sits in every row it fits by the brief’s own rule; both rows’ notes say the readings part and take no side.

worker_points.point: 5. Row 21: Israel’s kingdom and the kingdom of God; the rabbi’s seat especially
worker_points.why: The Exodus verse is filed under a New Testament lead, which is OT framing under rule 5 (fix 3). The taken-away and restored verses stay as the text has them.

worker_points.point: 6. Row 4: David’s throne; the Jewish reading
worker_points.why: The note names the Jewish reading and Christian readings as parting, takes no side, and keeps the 1 Chr 28:7 condition. Luke 1:33 and Mark 11:10 are the text’s own words for the promise and are not filed under a New Testament heading.

worker_points.point: 7. Rows 18 and 19: enter, inherit, “will not inherit”; John 3:5 and the vice lists
worker_points.why: The note states the readings of “born of water” and of whether the saved can fall short, names both and takes no side. The lists are the text’s words.
Two verses, kept as a row because the text sets them apart. The note names the readings of to whom the keys are given and of binding and loosing, and takes no side.
The note names what is said and takes no side on what the Supper is. It names no doctrine of the Supper, which is correct for this page.

worker_points.point: 10. Divine persons by hand: Heb 1:8 in row 9, Ps 45:6 in row 5
worker_points.why: Heb 1:8 in the Son row is the text’s own “about the Son”, and stays. Ps 45:6 is a king’s psalm in its own terms and moves to the king’s row (fix 4).
John 18:36 is a true “not” and stays. The row’s second member, Luke 17:21, is not a negation and comes out (fix 5).

worker_points.point: 12. Rows 2, 5 and 26: earthly kingdoms (Esth 5:3, Mark 6:23, Luke 4:5-6)
worker_points.why: The notes say only what the king offers and what the devil shows. The devil’s claim is the text’s own.

missing.what: “The LORD reigns” (the Hebrew verb מָלַךְ, the kingship of the LORD in the Psalms). The hub is noun-only by design and has no row for the verb. For the rabbi and for any reader of the Hebrew Scriptures the LORD’s kingship is the central claim, and the LORD row’s label “the LORD over every kingdom” does not carry it. Checked on the server: Ps 93:1 reads “The LORD reigns!”. The door to the theme card “The LORD reigns” is in the row and suffices if the note names the verb and these verses.

examples_checked: 27 of 27 rows: every row’s examples show their label; two are loose (1 Cor 15:24 in the still-ahead row; Luke 13:18, which asks what the kingdom of God is like, in the parables row)
summary: The hub is faithful to the text and its contested points are set side by side with notes that take no side, with rows 27 over the brief’s 25 justified by the two senses kept apart. Five placements need fixing (Rev 1:9, Luke 19 parable, Exod 19:6, Ps 45:6, Luke 17:21) and one note should name the verb “The LORD reigns”, and after those the hub could ship for all nine seats.
